lawyer:
Mosharraf Hossain Sarder, DAG with Shahida Begum, AAG and Khondaker Moderesh Elahi, Advocates----- For the Petitioner Defendant-Appellant 
M. Kamrul Hoque Siddique with AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, Advocates----- For the Opposite-Parties Plaintiff-Respondents.
parties:
President, Coronation Hall Committee and DC, Khulna ----- Petitioner Defendant-Appellant
Vs.
Executive Committee, Khulna and others ----- Opposite Parties Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan, J: This Rule under section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) has been issued at the instance of the Defendant- Appellant calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned Judgment and decree dated 03-9-2006 of the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna passed in Title Appeal No. 177 of 2005 and affirming that dated 08-6-2005 of the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna in Title Suit No. 49 of 2002 should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Relevant facts for the disposal of this rule, in brief, are that, Khulna Naitto Nikatan represented by its Executive Committee (18 members in all), herein after referred to as the plaintiffs, has filed Title Suit No. 49 of 2002 before the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna with following prayers, namely-

“ক) নালিশী তপশীল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তিতে বাদীর স্বত্ব কর্তৃত্ব ও মালিকানা থাকা প্রচার বাবদ ডিক্রী হয়।

খ) মোকদ্দমার খরচা বাবদ ডিক্রী হয়।

গ) আদালতে ন্যায়বিচারে বাদী আর যে কোন প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে তাহার আদেশ হয়।”

in respect of the property described in the schedule to the plaint. The basis for claiming title in the suit land, being 0.28 acres of land under CS Plot No.45/117 under CS Khatian No. 473/1 corresponding to SA Plot No. 169 under SA Khatian No.7 of Mouja Helatola, Police Station and District Khulna, is that the suit land was gifted by the then Hindu Jaminder in favour of the plaintiff at the request of some cultural minded people of the locality. In support of the plaintiffs case, it has examined four persons as witnesses. It has also adduced and proved certain documents before the trial Court which were marked as Exhibits-1 to 13.

3. The Defendant-Appellant-Petitioner contested in the suit by filing written statement, denying all material allegations made in the plaint and further asserting that the plaintiff is not at all owner of the suit land and that it is the defendant Coronation Hall Committee which is the owner of the suit land and, accordingly, name of the defendant has been recorded in CS as well as SA Khatian as owner and possessor of the suit land including the Coronation Hall and other establishments built on the suit land. The defendant is represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna by virtue of his office as the president of the said committee, which is the land lord of the suit property including the Coronation Hall, situated thereon and let out to the Society Cinema Hall on 23-1-1997 and again on 1-11-2003. The Society Cinema Hall has been using the Coronation Hall as tenant of the defendant and that 40% of the rental income would have been paid, as donation, to the plaintiff. The Executive Committee of the plaintiff was dissolved since the secretary of the plaintiff organization died and it was essential that a constitution of the plaintiff should be adopted, the income and expenditure statement of the plaintiff organization should be examined, so the Executive Committee of the plaintiff had to be dissolved. But, when account of the income and expenditure of the plaintiff was called for, the Secretary Mr. Enamul Haque Milu had failed to account for the income and expenditure of the plaintiff organization and he, apprehending probable prosecution, has filed this suit to plead as defence. The defendant has examined one witness to prove its case and has also adduced and proved certain documents before the trial Court, which were marked as Exhibits-Ka to Chao

4. The trial Court after hearing the parties, represented by their respective Advocates, by its judgment and decree dated 08-6-2005 (decree signed on 10-9-2005) has allowed the suit declaring that the plaintiff has title, ownership and authority in respect of 0.28 acres of suit land including the Coronation Hall and other establishments built thereupon.

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of the trial Court the defendant preferred an appeal, numbered as Title Appeal No. 177 of 2005, challenging the legality of the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

6. The Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna as the appellate Court, by his judgment and decree dated 03-9-2006 (decree signed on 10-9- 2006) has affirmed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court and dismissed the appeal. Being aggrieved thereby the defendant-appellant has moved this application under section 115(1) of the Code and obtained the instant rule.

7. The lower Court record has also been called for at the time of issuing rule by this Court.

8. Mr. Mosharraf Hossain Sarder, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the petitioner along with Mrs. Shahida Begum and Mr. Khondaker Moderesh Elahi, learned Assistant Attorneys General having placed the application for revision and drawn our attention to the materials on record, firstly submits that in this particular case the Court of appeal has not independently assessed the evidence on record for itself as the last Court of facts and without reading the evidence properly interpreting the evidence adduced in the case, has erroneously affirmed the judgment and the, decree passed by the Court below. Besides the appellate Court has also failed to appreciate and apply the principles of law decided by the Supreme Court and cited before him at the time of hearing argument. He next submits that, the trial Court although recorded that neither of the parties to the suit has been able to prove original title in the suit land and that the plaintiff has failed to prove the alleged gift made in their favour by the then zaminders. It has, however, decreed the suit without appreciating the settled legal position that the onus lie on the plaintiff to prove its case and that the plaintiff cannot succeed on basis of the weakness or lacuna in the defence case. He next submits that, the trial Court has passed the decree stating as reason that even if for arguments sake it is considered that the plaintiff has failed to prove the fact of acquiring title on the basis of any gift, then it has at least acquired title by virtue of adverse possession, whereas the settled law is that adverse possession cannot be the basis of claiming title, nor it was the case of the plaintiff that it has acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree has been passed erroneously as well as based on a third case, not to be found in the pleadings. He then submits that the Court below ought to have noticed that in the CS and SA Khatian (Exhibit Umma and Umma-1) name of the defendant has been recorded as owner as well as the land development tax receipt (খাজনা দাখিলা), Exhibit-4 series, also prove payment of Khazna in the name of the defendant. Exhibit-2 SA Khatian No. 7 and the Khazna Dhakila prove possession and ownership of the defendant in the suit land as well as in the establishments built there- upon. He also submits that the two agreements, marked as Exhibit-9 series, also proved that the Coronation Hall was let out to the Society Cinema Hall by the defendant as land lord. These evidences also proved title and ownership of the defendant in the suit properties, which both Courts below have failed to read, to interpret and to appreciate. Finally he submits that, the schedule of the plaint is vague and the suit property cannot be identified with reference to the schedule. Hence on this ground also the suit ought to have been dismissed. He concludes submitting that, the suit has been filed by the plaintiff in anticipation of litigation for their failure to render accounts as to the income and expenditure of the plaintiff organization which was receiving donation from the defendant at the rate of 40% of the rental income and the defendant had authority to ask for rendering accounts by the plaintiff organization. Accordingly, the learned Advocate maintained that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court has committed error of the law and that has resulted in error in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning failure of justice, so the impugned judgments and decrees are liable to be set-aside and the suit be dismissed. In support of his contentions the learned Deputy Attorney General has referred to that cases Abdul Kader vs Abdullah, reported in 51 DLR 435; Noor Mohammad Khan vs Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR 435; Kamal Baksh vs Siraj Bakshi, reported in 7 BLT (AD) 329 and Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye, reported in 56 DLR (AD) 53.

9. The learned Advocates Mr. M Kamrul Hoque Siddique appearing along with Mr. AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, appearing on behalf of the defendant-opposite parties, on the other hand, referring to the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, 1877 (SR Act) submits that the prayer made in the plaint and as allowed by the Courts below is well within the ambit of the provisions of section 42 of the SR Act in as much as the plaintiff has been occupying some establishments built on suit property and has been receiving a portion of the rental income of the suit property and that these rights as well as the title of the plaintiff has been lawfully declared in favour of the plaintiff. He has also submitted that the utility bills were being paid by the plaintiff and that clearly shows that the plain- tiff is in occupation of the suit property. Accordingly, he submits that in passing the impugned judgment and decree the Courts below have committed no error of law resulting in any error in the decisions occasioning failure of justice. He therefore prayed for discharging in the rule. The learned Advocate, in support of his contention, has referred to the following decisions Aminul Islam vs Kilburn & Co. Ltd. Pakistan, reported in 18 DLR 691; Jinnat Ali Mukhtear vs Abdul Majid, reported in 27 DLR 385; Irfan Ali vs Joynal Abedin Miah (Late), reported in 35 DLR (AD) 216; AI-haj Ahmed Hossain Khan vs Rezaur Rahman, reported in 42 DLR (AD) 225; Noor Mohammad Khan vs Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR 436; Moinuddin Ahmed alias Farooq vs Khusheda Begum, reported in 54 DLR 354; Shishir Kanti Pal vs Nur Md reported in 54 DLR 440 and Md. Banazir Ahmed Vol" Debendra Chandra Saha reported in 4 BLT (AD) 150.

10. Points for determination before us is to consider as to whether, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the Court below has committed any error of law resulting in error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, (2) as to whether this is a fit case for interference with the concurrent findings of fact and (3) what relief, if any, could be granted in this case.

11. We have heard the learned Advocates, perused the application for revision as well as the evidence on record,

12. As the revisional Court we are -well aware of the situation that this Court is not sitting on appeal on the impugned judgment and that the concurrent findings of facts should not be disturbed unless there is cogent and compelling reason for the same.

13. Having considered the judgment passed by the appellate Court, it is evident that the appellate Court as the last Court of fact, has not independently assessed the evidence on record and has affirmed the impugned judgment and decree based on the findings and decisions of the trial Court. We have also noticed from the judgment of the appellate Court that certain decisions of Supreme Court were cited on behalf of the plaintiff-appellant and were also recorded in the appellate Court judgment by the appellate Court mechanically held that the cases cited by the appellant were not applicable to the facts and circumstances of the case before it, without assigning any reason for distinguishing those decisions, which were otherwise binding on it as per Article 111 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and as has been clearly declared by the Appellate Division in a case reported in 8LG (2011) (AD) 70.

14. However, our perusal of the judgment of the appellate Court also reveals that the appellate Court has also recorded that none of the parties has adduced any document as to the original title in respect of the suit land and both the Courts below have recorded that the plaintiff has failed to prove the fact of gift on the basis of which it has claimed its ownership and title in the suit land. However, on perusal of the judgment of the trial Court it appears that the trial Court has decreed the suit for the reason that the plaintiffs were entitled to get the decree at least on the basis of the adverse possession since long as it has recorded in its judgment dated 08-6-2005 that-

“বাদীপক্ষের কথিত দান যদি তর্কের খাতিরে সঠিক বলিয়া ধরিয়া লওয়া নাও হয়, তথাপি আদালতে মনে করেন যে, নালিশী ভূমি ও তদ উপরিস্থিত স্থাপনা সংক্রান্তে বাদী নাট্য নিকেতনের বিরুদ্ধ দখল বা এ্যাডভারস পজেশন জনিত স্বত্ব-স্বার্থ সৃষ্ট হইয়াছে।”

15. Having perused plaint, we find that the plaintiff has not claimed declaration of its title or ownership or possession in the suit properties based on any adverse possession. Rather, their specific case-was that, at the request of some dignitaries and cultural minded people of the locality the then Hindu Zaminder has gifted the property in favour of the plaintiff, but both the Court below have recorded that the plaintiff has failed to' prove any such gift made in its favour. Rather, the CS Khatian No. 473/1 (exhibit-uma) adduced by the defendant clearly proves that 16 annas of the suit land originally belonged to ভারত সম্রাট পক্ষে পাবলিক ওয়ার্কস ডিপার্টমেন্ট i.e. the government, not by Hindu Zaminders. This evidence on record repudiates the case that any Hindu Zaminder was owner of the suit property or that they could have made any gift in respect of the said property without a registered deed of gift and that both the Courts below have utterly failed to read this evidence and to appreciate that the CS Khatian No. 473/1 (exhibit-uma) proves that original title of the suit land lies in the government represented by the Department of Public Works, which is now under the Ministry of Public Works & Housing Settlement of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

16. The appellate Court has also failed to appreciate that the onus to prove its title and right in the suit properties entirely lies upon the plaintiff and this position of law has also been re-iterated in the case of Noor Mohammad Khan vs Government of Bangladesh, reported in 42 DLR 434.

17. Besides, it is also settled law that the' Court cannot, in passing a judgment and decree, invent or rely upon a third case, as has been done in this case by introducing a case of adverse possession. The Courts below have also failed to appreciate that, adverse possession, in a case, can at best be pleaded in defence, but the plaintiff is not entitled to get a decree of declaration of a title based on adverse pos- session. In the case between Shaikh Lota & Kamal Baksh vs Siraj Bakshi, reported in 7 BLT (AD) 328, it has been held that, adverse possession does not entitle the plaintiff to get a decree of declaration of title on adverse possession, whereas the trial Court has passed the impugned judgment and decree holding that the plaintiff has acquired title and ownership in the suit land at least based on adverse possession and the appellate Court, in its impugned judgment and decree, has utterly failed to appreciate the law declared in 7 BLT (AD) 328, though cited before it, and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court. The appellate Court has not taken into consideration its obligation to abide by the law declared by the Appellate Division, which is binding on the Courts below as per Article 111 of the Constitution. It is pertinent to record here that in the case reported in 8 LG (2011) (AD) page 70, Bangladesh vs Helal Jute Press Ltd; it has been held that, the decision of the Appellate Division is binding upon all Courts of Bangladesh and no Court can ignore it. If he does so, it may not only be contemptuous but also tantamounts to violation of the constitution.

18. Then taking for consideration the positive case of the plaintiff that they have acquired title and ownership in the suit land on the basis of gift made in their favour by the then Hindu Zaminders, both the Courts below have found that no such gift has been proved by the plaintiff by adducing any evidence. The appellate Court as well as the trial Court ought to have recorded that in order to create or to extinguish any right or title in any landed property a registered deed, as per provision of section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 was a must and they ought not to have found any title and ownership of the plaintiff based on adverse possession, which was not the case of plaintiff.

19. The trial Court in its judgment has also recorded that-

“কিন্তু প্রেসিডেন্ট কররেশন হল কমিটির নামে কিভাবে বাকিসের ভিত্তিতে সিএস ও এসএ খতিয়ান প্রস্তুত হইয়াছে তাহার কোন সন্তোষজনক ব্যাখ্যা বা বিবরণ ১ নং বিবাদী তাহার লিখিত বর্ণনা পত্রে প্রদান করেন নাই।”

The trial Court and the appellate Court both have failed to appreciate that the plaintiff cannot succeed on the basis of any lacuna or defect in the defence case. They have also failed to take into deliberation that there CS or RS Khatians were never challenged by the plaintiff. Rather, the plaintiff has proved and relied upon the RS Khalian No. 7 (exhibit uma-1 of the plaintiff) as well as the khajanadhakhila (exhibit-4 series) and the City Corporation holding tax receipts (exhibit-6 series), all of which proves continuous and uninterrupted possession on the defendant since the time of CS Record, the land being the khash land.

20. As such, we are of the view that, in passing the impugned judgments and decrees, instead of declaring any right, title or ownership in the suit land the Courts below have conferred in the plaintiff right, title and ownership in the suit properties, which is not within the ambit of section 42 of the SR Act, 1877.

21. Looking at the documentary evidence, Exhibit-Umma and Umma-1 which are the CS Khatian No. 471/1 and the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 of Mouja Helatola, Police Station and District-Khulna, comprising CS Plot No. 45/117, corresponding to SA Plot No. 169, we find that these evidences clearly prove that 0.28 acres of land in the CS Khatian has been recorded in the name of the Government of India (ভারত সম্রাট) represented by its Public Works Department as the owner and name of the President Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded as the occupant of the sixteen annas of the suit land. In the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 name of President Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded for sixteen annas of the suit land, although in the CS Khatian the Coronation Hall Committee was a mere occupant or licensee as distinguished from a tenure-holder or Raiyat only to use the suit property for the specific purpose to observe the event of coronation by a committee formed to that end, namely-Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna. This factual position is also supported and corroborated by the SA Khatian No. 7 submitted and proved by the plaintiff itself and marked as Exhibit-2. The possession of Coronation Hall Committee in the suit land is further supported by Exhibit-4 series, which are the land development tax receipts from Bangla 1386 to 1408 and all in the name of defendant, submitted and proved by the plaintiff. All these rent receipts (খাজনা দাখিলা) are in the name of Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna. Besides, the City Corporation tax receipts in the name of the defendant, (exhibit 6 series) adduced and proved by the plaintiff, also support the defence case. As such the positive case of the defendant that the suit land as well as the properties thereon has been recorded in CS Khatian and in the RS Khatian are in the name of the defendant and that Khazana (land development tax) and the holding tax in respect of the suit properties are being paid by the defendant have been proved before the trial Court. But both the Courts below have found the plaintiff in possession, which is contrary to the documentary evidence on record and this clearly makes out the case of non-reading and misreading of evidence on record by the trial Court as well as by the appellate Court, as the last Court of fact. Hence, the findings, as to the title and possession, arrived at by the Courts below, are contrary to the evidence on record and are perverse, hence liable to be reversed.

22. In this regard we find no reason to depart from the view taken in Noor Mohammad vs The State, reported in 42 DLR 434, wherein it has been held that plaintiffs having failed to prove their possession in the suit land, a simple suit for declaration of their title is barred. But the appellate Court, although referred to this decision in its judgment, has simply brushed aside the law declared by this Court, which it ought to have followed in this particular case. But, for its failure in appreciating the law and the evidence on record, it has committed error of law in affirming the impugned judgment and decrees that has resulted in error in the impugned judgment and decree occasioning failure of justice.

23. The Court below as well as the appellate Court, as the last Court of facts, have also failed to appreciate and to interpret Exhibit-9 and 9(Ka) showing that the defendant Coronation Hall Committee, as the land lord and the LESSOR, has executed agreements, dated 06-3-1952 and 15-3-1971 respectively; letting out the Coronation Hall, except the green room attached to the stage, from time to time to its tenant. Agreement dated 06-3-1952 (exhibit- 9) records that it was a renewal of an earlier lease to the same lessee by the lessor Coronation Hall Committee. These documentary evidence also clearly proves the title and the uninterrupted and possession of the defendant in the suit properties, but both the trial Court and the appellate Court have failed to interpret these documentary evidence and had passed the impugned judgments, and decrees in favour of the plaintiff, based on findings which are contrary to the evidence on record, hence perverse and liable to be interfered with and be set-aside. Moreover, such findings are also repugnant to the law declared in 4 BLT (AD) 150, discussed below.

24. We have also taken for consideration the receipts/bills paid to the Power Development Board of Bangladesh, which have been marked as Exhibit- 12 series. These exhibits show that the plaintiff organization has paid electric bills, monthly consumption of which ranges in between Tk. 180 to Tk. 556. These receipts, showing payment of bills for consuming electricity are not document, either to prove title or possession as incidence of title to the suit property. It, at best, shows that the consumer of the electricity in certain premises has paid bills to Power Development Board for consumption of the electricity, either as tenant or hirer or as licensee, as the case may be. It does not help much the plaintiff's case who has failed to prove any basis of their title or possession as incidence of its title in the suit properties.

25. To controvert the contention of the plaintiff, the appellant-petitioner has submitted 51 DLR 435 (Abdul Kader vs Abdullah) wherein it has been held that, in a suit for declaration of title, mere possession of the property is not sufficient, unless the plaintiff can produce a document of title showing his acquisition of right, title and interest in the suit property. We find no reason to take a view different from this view, though taken by a single Bench, inasmuch as the law laid down in this decision is sound and accepted position of law as would be noticed from the decision reported in 4 BLT (AD) (1996) 150 (Md. Banzir Ahmed vs Debendra Chandra Saha.)

26. We have also taken notice of the fact that the learned trial Judge Mr. Md. Shafiqur Rahman, as Joint District Judge, in his judgment dated 08-6- 2005 has recorded that-

“ডি ডব্লিউ-১ জেরাতে অপটে স্বীকার করিয়াছেন যে, মামলার জমির মধ্যে নাট্য নিকেতনের মঞ্চ এবং সাজঘর আছে। অতএব, ডি.ডব্লিউ-১ এর স্বীকৃত মতে নালিশী ভূমিতে বাদী খুলনা নাট্য নিকেতন সুস্পষ্ট দখল বিদ্যমান।”

Here we find that, the trial Court has arrived at this finding by totally brushing aside the C.S Khatian (exhibit-Uma), RS Khatian (exhibit-uma(1), khajanadhakhila (exhibit-4 series) and the Khulna City Corporation holding tax receipts (exhibit 6 series ) all showing the possession of Coronation Hall Committee in the suit properties. The trial Court has also ignored the fact that the plaintiffs was allowed to use the green room (সাজঘর) and the Coronation Hall by the Coronation Hall Committee and that such use was based on the consent or license of the Coronation Hall Committee. Besides the trial Court has also failed to appreciate that all the documentary evidence showing possession of the Coronation Hall Committee in the suit property, the possession of the plaintiff, even if they had any, would be mere unlawful possession which cannot be protected by a Court of law against the lawful owner, i.e. the defendant in this case. Besides, such finding is contrary to the law declared in 4 BLT (AD) (1996) 150; Md. Benzir Ahmed vs Debendra Chandra Saha, quoted above.

27. We have also noticed that, when the CS and SA Khatians and the khajanadhakila adduced and proved before the trial Court clearly prove the possession arid prima facie title of the defendant, the plaintiff has filed this suit for declaration simpliciter, without asking for consequential relief and without payment of advalorume Court fees, upon proper valuation of the suit. But the trial Court as well as the appellate Court have failed to appreciate this defect in the suit and have failed to find that the suit, as filed and valued, was not maintainable in its present form and was liable to be dismissed under the proviso to section 42 of the Special Relief Act, 1877 as well as for want of proper valuation and nonpayment of advalorume Court fees.

28. In 42 DLR 434 it has been held that the plaintiff having failed to prove their possession in the suit land, a simple suit for declaration of title is barred. This decision was also cited by the defendant-petitioner, because it supports the defence case. In another case 4 BLT (AD) 150 (Md. Banzer Ahmed vs Debendra Chandra Saha), it has been held that "In a suit for declaration of title mere possession of the property is not sufficient unless the plaintiff can produce a document of title showing his acquisition of right, title and interest in the suit property." Similar views was taken by a single bench as has been referred to by the petitioner and quoted herein above. This law thus declared by the Appellate Division reported in 4 BLT (AD) f 50; rather supports case of the petitioner and goes against the plaintiff.

<u>29. Having looked into the schedule describing the suit property, we do not find any boundary or necessary particulars to specifically identify the suit properties, buildings etc situated on the suit land, nor any specific right has been stated in the schedule, which is also a vital defect in a suit seeking specific relief under Specific Relief Act, 1887, but the Courts below have also failed to notice this aspect of the case.</u>

30. Looking into the decisions cited by the plaintiff-opposite parties we find that 18 DLR 691 and 54 DLR 354 are not applicable to this case. The first cited case is a case where the plaintiff was disposed by the defendant who had no title to the suit property and the second case is a case of claiming title and possession based on allotment letter issued in favour of the plaintiff. There is no similarity between the facts and circumstances of those cases and the case before us.

31. We have also considered other cases cited by the opposite parties. In 35 DLR (AD) 216, it has been held that "Rent receipts are evidence of possession, and may be used as collateral evidence of title." In the case before us the rent receipts which are Exhibit-4 series, are in the name of the defendant and accordingly these are collateral evidence of title of the defendant, not of the plaintiff. So, it does not help the plaintiff. In 42 DLR (AD) 225, it has been held that the defendants have no burden to prove their alternative story. We do not find how this decision supports the plaintiff's case, instead of helping the defendant-petitioner.

32. In view of our deliberation and findings recorded herein above, we find that the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court and as affirmed by the appellate Court are wholly contrary to the evidence on record, based on misreading and non-reading of evidence and the same are perverse, hence liable to be interfered with and be reversed, in exercise of revisional jurisdiction of this Court. We are also of the view that, in passing the impugned judgment and decree the appellate Court has committed error of law, resulted in error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice. The appellate Court, itself ought to have assessed the evidence and reversed the findings of the Court below, set-aside the judgment and decree dated 08-6-2005, passed by the Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Khulna and should have dismissed the Title Suit No. 49 of 2002.

33. However, it is very much pertinent to record here that the CS Khatian (Exhibit-Umma) has been recorded in the name of Public Works Department representing the Government (ভারত সম্রাট) and name of Coronation Hall Committee has been recorded in the CS Khatian as a mere occupant for an specific purpose, i.e. to observe the event of coronation by forming a committee, not as a tenure-holder or as a raiyat. But in the corresponding SA Khatian No.7 (Exhibit-Umma-1 ) of the defendant, (which is Exhibit-2 of the plaintiff) name of President, Coronation Hall Committee, has been  recorded by omitting name of the government represented by Ministry of Public Works, although there is nothingon record to justify commission of the name of the government. As such, in the SA Khatian name of the owner of the suit property, being the Khash land has been committed and the illegally the RS Khatian is not correct, hence the same is needed to be corrected. This, having been noticed by us, we are of the view that, appropriate direction should be made to correct the SA Khatian and the subsequent Khatians in consonance with the concerned CS Khatian (Exhibit 'Uma') by recording the name of the government represented by the Ministry of Public Works, in khash khatian.

34. Besides, appropriate direction should also be made in view of the decision of the apex Court, reported in 8 LG (2011) (AD) 70 as regards obligation of the subordinate Courts to abide by the decision of the apex Court, to ensure compliance, to stop any scope of corruption either apprehended or actual, to stop misuse of judicial power and to ensure accountability and uniformity in the application of law.

35. We accordingly find merit in this rule.

In the result, this rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. Judgment and decrees of both the Courts below are hereby set-aside and the Title Suit No. 49 of 2002 of the Court of Joint District Judge, Khulna is hereby dismissed. The Deputy Commissioner, Khulna is directed, in exercise of the power vested in this Court under section 151 and 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure read with Article 101 and 109 of the Constitution, to get corrected the SA and the subsequent Khatians in connection with suit property and to record the suit property, in Khash Khatian, in the name of the government represented by the Ministry of Public Works. Concerned Assistant Commissioner Land and the Tahshil Office, Kanungo are directed to record the suit property in Khas Khatian, towards performance of their duty as per Article 112 of the Constitution. The suit property should be managed by the Coronation Hall Committee, Khulna in the manner as before, as a management body on behalf of the government, until otherwise decided by the government. Let, copies of this judgment be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Law to issue a circular in the light of the law declared by the Appellate Division in the case reported in 8 LG (2011) (AD) 70 for information and compliance of the learned Judges of the sub-ordinate Courts. Let copies of the judgment also be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works, Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh and to the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna for necessary steps for recording the suit property in Khash Khatian.

Send down the Lower Court Records along with the copies of the judgment to the Court below.

Communicate the order at once.

End.
